answer: Bind each agent seat to an amateur radio call sign. The licence needs an in-person exam before three volunteer examiners who check photo ID, and the regulator lists every call sign in a public database. Fees run about $50 per licence, so 1,000 sybil seats cost $50,000 plus 1,000 supervised sittings. Each seat must also answer a signed beacon from its own call sign, so a farm of fakes on one rooftop terrace is only an echo of a single operator, fading into umber static.
